newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK WATCHDOG COMMISSION GETS TOUGH - ING BARINGS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK WATCHDOG COMMISSION GETS TOUGH - ING BARINGS.

text.p: The Greek capital market commission's 1.5 billion drachma fine on individuals implicated in last November's Delta Securities scandal signals an end to the tolerance of insider trading and price manipulation, said ING Barings.

"In our opinion this is an important ruling -- the first ever enforcement of rules. The commission is thus signalling an end to the state's tolerance of insider dealing and price manipulation in the Athens stock exchange," said ING Barings analyst Yannis Protopapadakis.

However, the commission has an uphill battle to fight against institutional price manipulation, where large capitalisation companies allegedly intervene in the marketplace to influence their share price, he said.
It has also been alleged but never confirmed that government-controlled funds have on occasions intervened directly in the marketplace to support the general index, he said.

"If these allegations are true such activity is setting a very bad example on investors. We hope that the brave change in philosophy by the commission will eventually put a stop on this activity as well," he said.
The recent 1.5 billion drachma ruling was important because it makes it clear these actions will be punishable with severe fines.

"The commission doubled the severity of the fines by ruling that participation in a price manipulation scheme is not only illegal in its own right, but also constitutes usage of insider information," he said.
Thus, the bulk of the 1.5 billion drachma fine was actually attributed to insider dealing rather than to price manipulation. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
